title: The GDPR Notification Letter (Google Doc)
description:
Draft the letter Sankofa Digital will file with its lead supervisory authority under **Article 33 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)**. You have **72 hours** from the moment of discovery — the clock started at 04:12 UTC on 2024-01-15, so the filing deadline is **04:12 UTC / 05:12 WAT on 2024-01-18**. The IR report (Stage 3 task 7) flagged Article 33 applicability; this is the letter that follows.

**Submission via Google Doc link.** This letter is a formal legal artefact — letterhead, addressing block, body paragraphs, signature line. Create a Google Doc, set sharing to **'Anyone with the link → Viewer'**, paste the URL below with a 75+ word abstract.

**The letter must:**

  •  State the **data controller's name** and the **DPO's name + contact** (you may invent reasonable placeholders, but the role titles must be correct under GDPR — Data Controller, Data Protection Officer).
  •  State the **categories** and approximate **volume** of affected data subjects, anchored in what Stage 2 task 1 revealed about the exposed Elasticsearch indices (`customer_pii` ~84,210 docs; `transaction_log` ~1.2M records; `intern_access` 3 docs). Do not inflate.
  •  State the **nature of the breach** in plain language (≤3 sentences).
  •  State the **exact filing deadline** in UTC and WAT, and whether this draft is before or after that deadline.
  •  State the **consequences** and the **containment actions already taken** (mirror Stage 3 task 7 §5 Containment).
  •  State the **remediation roadmap** (reference Stage 4 task 4 — the 30/60/90 — if you have completed it; otherwise summarise the 0–30 window).
  •  Identify whether **affected data subjects must also be notified** under GDPR Article 34, and on what timeline.
  •  **Sign off** in a form that would be defensible if quoted in court (name, role, date, contact).
  •  Add a short **assumptions and unknowns** paragraph: what is confirmed, what is still under evidence-locker review, and what update you will send the supervisory authority if the count changes.

**Avoid:**
- Unnecessary hedging.
- Legalese you cannot define if asked.
- Figures you cannot support with evidence from the investigation. A letter that misstates facts is worse than a late letter.

**Citation bar:**
- **GDPR Article 33** cited with the 72-hour clock referenced.
- **GDPR Article 34** for data-subject notification (if applicable).
- **EDPB Guidelines 9/2022 on personal data breach notification** or an official supervisory-authority breach-notification guide for any procedural step you describe.
- One reference to **NIST SP 800-61r2** for the IR alignment.
- The IR report (Stage 3 task 7) cited as the source of facts.
- `07-board-minutes-excerpt.md` cited for the conservative affected-count decision.

**One mistake I almost made (in the Doc, 60+ words):** the seductive wrong answer is over-stating volumes (`~1.3M affected subjects`) by counting `transaction_log` rows as data subjects when they are transaction records that likely overlap fewer unique subjects. Or under-counting by ignoring `intern_access` because the row count is small (the *sensitivity* of credential-adjacent data may matter more than the count). Name the specific framing decision you nearly miswrote and how you corrected it.

**Minimum 700 words in the Doc.** Paste link + 75+ word abstract below.

**Regulator update commitment (mandatory, 50+ words):** Include one paragraph explaining what would trigger a supplemental notice to the supervisory authority after the offline evidence locker is reconciled, who owns that update, and the maximum time you would allow before sending it. Do not name Amaka in the Article 33 letter unless you can justify why the identity is necessary to explain the breach; if you omit her name, state how you will preserve honesty without prejudging the investigation.

This is a board-visible artefact — it will be quoted back at you if the investigation concludes differently. Write it accordingly.

---

**Universal grading rule.** Generic answers fail. Every claim in your submission must be tied to specific evidence — an artefact from the lab (file path, log line, command output, payload, screenshot) **and** at least one external citation where research is relevant (NIST section number, MITRE technique ID, CVE, vendor advisory, ISO control ID, GDPR article). Claims without an attached artefact, timestamp, payload, standard section, or business constraint earn zero for that claim. Lab-only answers earn partial credit. External-only answers earn partial credit. Full credit requires both.
